summary: This week's signals concentrate on settlement and standards infrastructure, and on live-hardware validation of quantum algorithms for the grid. On the RWA side, the Swiss National Bank on 24 November launched a Swiss Financial Ledger exploration project with UBS, SIX, Zürcher Kantonalbank and others (explicitly not a decision to launch the ledger or to issue tokenised central-bank money); the Federal Council on 25 November approved 57 partner jurisdictions for automatic exchange of crypto-asset information (from 2028); the ECB on 24 November released a Tokenisation Reference Model for the European Tokenisation Standards Group; the Hong Kong Monetary Authority on 25 November formally launched the CMU Digital Asset Platform, supporting bond tokenisation and 24-hour multi-currency DvP settlement, with plans to extend to funds and real-world assets; and the US OKXICE tokenised-securities venue went live on 23 November under an SEC "innovation exemption", with 113 assets confirmed in the first batch. On the quantum-energy side, a quantum electromagnetic-transient simulation method from Origin Quantum, Southeast University and NARI was validated on Origin Wukong-180 with 2 qubits (paper in IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Energy); the Wuhan Quantum Forum on 24 November released ten quantum application scenarios, including grid-connection testing of a quantum current transformer and photonic-radar wind-power forecasting. Fusion this week was mainly engineering and supply chain: the UK STEP programme awarded a £6.84 million gyrotron design contract, Proxima Fusion completed manufacture of the first stellarator radial plate, and Tennessee's first IRIS grant of $5.8 million went to tritium-breeding materials. No verified large new energy-asset RWA issuance was found this week.
trends: Tokenisation infrastructure has entered a stage of "central-bank-grade platforms + common standards": in the same week, the Swiss National Bank launched exploration of a Swiss Financial Ledger (24 November), the ECB released a Tokenisation Reference Model (24 November), and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority formally launched the CMU Digital Asset Platform (25 November). Added to last week's SG Digital Ledger in Singapore, four major financial centres are writing tokenisation into core financial infrastructure.

The United States is taking an "exemption first" path: OKXICE went live on 23 November, with 113 assets confirmed in the first batch, and the SEC list shows TSV operating notices from five firms; but 67 issuers have filed objection notices, and issuer consent is becoming the main constraint.

Quantum energy: live-hardware validation of algorithms is increasing, but scale is still small. Electromagnetic-transient simulation on Origin Wukong-180 used 2 qubits. CNBC (22 November) reported that Phasecraft said software developed with UK grid operator NESO was "up to 1,000 times faster" on some tasks; LetzView (24 November) noted that this figure is a company-reported compute speed, with no disclosed comparison baseline, and is not a measured improvement in grid operations.

Energy RWAs still lack large, audited new issues: on-chain data site XRP Sonar (26 November) recorded a new issue of 7,347,450 JMWH power-contract tokens from YPF Luz/Justoken on 24 November (each token corresponding to 1 MWh), but also noted that the dollar amount implied by an RWA.xyz valuation is not a market price, and that the ledger itself cannot prove the underlying contracts and cash flows. Such data can only be observed, and should not be cited as evidence of scale.

Fusion funding and supply chains continue to "engineer": a UK STEP gyrotron contract of £6.84 million, Tennessee IRIS funding of $5.8 million (1:1 matched), and $1.48 million for fusion technician training in California. New funding this week is mainly for components, the fuel cycle and talent.

To watch next week: China Southern Power Grid's "power-market clearing simulation research based on quantum computing" project (budget 2.775 million yuan) opened bids on 27 November, with the award still to be published; the standstill period on the UK STEP gyrotron contract ends on 4 December; the US DOE quantum–HPC testbed RFI closes on 17 December.
footer: All facts and figures in this brief are taken from the public sources listed. The SNB has made clear that the Swiss Financial Ledger project does not represent a decision to launch the ledger or to issue tokenised central-bank money; the ECB TRM is a non-binding discussion framework; OKXICE operates under a temporary SEC exemption and is not a registered exchange; Phasecraft's "1,000 times" figure and the JMWH valuation are company-reported or third-party website estimates. The journal online date of the Origin Quantum paper should be taken from the IEEE page (the Crossref DOI was registered on 2026-11-06; media reports were on 11-23). Institutions mentioned are an observation list only and do not constitute any investment or partnership recommendation. Time window: 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-27 (Zurich time).

items.tag: Quantum computing × power grid · peer reviewed
items.title: Origin Quantum, Southeast University and NARI: quantum electromagnetic-transient simulation validated on Origin Wukong-180 hardware, reproducing grid waveforms with 2 qubits
items.what: According to China News Service (23 November) and Science and Technology Daily (24 November), a joint team from Origin Quantum, Southeast University and NARI proposed a "condition-number-aware" quantum electromagnetic-transient simulation (QEMTP) method: first identifying how ill-conditioned the grid equations are and applying targeted preconditioning, then using a specialised quantum optimisation strategy to ease the "trainability problem" of vanishing gradients and slow convergence in quantum algorithms. The method was validated on the fourth-generation domestic superconducting quantum computer Origin Wukong-180, reproducing voltage and current waveforms in close agreement with classical simulation using only 2 qubits (traditional schemes need 3). Reports put the deviation on the order of one part in 10 billion, and the number of iterations in the initial step fell from 28 to 7. The paper, "Towards Conditioning-Wise Quantum Electromagnetic Transient Simulation for Converter-Dominated Systems", appears in IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Energy (DOI: 10.1109/TSTE.2026.3751404).
items.why: Electromagnetic-transient simulation is one of the most computationally stressed steps after large-scale connection of renewables and power-electronic converters. This is a peer-reviewed, live-hardware validation on domestic superconducting quantum hardware, with a grid company's participation. The validation, however, is only a small case of 2 qubits — a proof of methodological feasibility, still far from practical acceleration of large-scale grid simulation.
items.src: China News Service / Science and Technology Daily (reprinted by China Daily online) / IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Energy

items.tag: Quantum sensing × new energy · application scenarios
items.title: Wuhan Quantum Forum 2026 releases ten quantum application scenarios, including grid-connection testing of a quantum current transformer and photonic-radar wind-power forecasting
items.what: According to Hubei Daily (reprinted by CRI Online, 25 November), Wuhan Quantum Forum 2026 on 24 November released ten quantum application scenarios, covering energy and power, biomedicine, geological exploration, meteorological new energy, intelligent connected vehicles and transport emergencies. Energy-related scenarios include: a full-scale environmental simulation test for a quantum current transformer, built by Wuhan NARI of the State Grid Electric Power Research Institute, to examine new quantum power equipment under simulated real grid conditions and to gate its safe connection to the grid; and a photonic-radar meteorological monitoring and wind-farm power-forecasting scenario built by Hubei Tianhong Testing Technology Group and Hubei Zhongke Guoguang Quantum Technology, using single-photon precision detection to keep observing the wind field in rain and fog. More than ten academicians, including Ye Chaohui and Zhu Shining, attended the opening.
items.why: Quantum precision measurement is moving from single-point demonstrations toward a system of grid-connection testing: quantum current transformers need standardised grid-connection inspection before they can be procured at grid scale, and wind-power forecasting bears directly on the stability of renewable connection. The report does not disclose specific figures for accuracy gains, and should be treated as a scenario release rather than a validation of results.

items.title: The Swiss National Bank, with UBS, SIX and others, launches a Swiss Financial Ledger exploration project; the Federal Council approves 57 partner jurisdictions for automatic exchange of crypto-asset information
items.what: On 24 November the Swiss National Bank (SNB), together with UBS, SIX, Zürcher Kantonalbank, PostFinance, Banque Cantonale Vaudoise, Basler Kantonalbank, Sygnum Bank and the settlement platform Seturion, announced the launch of a Swiss Financial Ledger exploration project. The project sits under Project Helvetia and follows on from the BIS/IIF Agorá project, studying whether a scheme that lets central-bank money, commercial-bank money and securities interact on the same DLT platform can serve both cross-border and domestic transactions, with a focus on technical architecture, governance and an operating framework, and with a Helvetia strategy committee established (the Swiss Bankers Association as observer). The SNB stated clearly that the project should not be understood as a decision to launch such a ledger or to issue tokenised central-bank money to financial institutions. On 25 November the Federal Council approved 57 countries and regions as partner jurisdictions for automatic exchange of information (AEOI) on crypto-assets, including all EU member states, the United Kingdom and several G20 countries, with exchange from 2028 with jurisdictions that have expressed interest and that meet OECD standards.
items.why: Switzerland is moving in tokenised settlement infrastructure from Helvetia wholesale-CBDC pilots toward a feasibility study of an industry-wide shared ledger, while aligning with the EU on tax transparency under the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). The Swiss RWA path is therefore one of infrastructure exploration and compliance transparency together.
items.src: Swiss National Bank / State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF)

items.title: The ECB releases a Tokenisation Reference Model (TRM) as input for a common rulebook from the European Tokenisation Standards Group
items.what: On 24 November the European Central Bank released a Tokenisation Reference Model (TRM), offering a structured framework for discussion with market participants on how to define a common rulebook and shared standards. The TRM lists law, governance, semantics, operations and infrastructure as areas in which a common framework can be built, and proposes five key capabilities for a tokenisation ecosystem: interoperability, transferability, portability (assets and their meaning can migrate in full), controllability and composability. The ECB said the framework will serve as input to the work of the recently announced European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG).
items.why: The ETSG membership call tracked last week closed on 27 November, and the ECB has promptly provided a discussion draft. EU tokenisation is moving from dispersed pilots toward common standards. The model itself is not legally binding, but it is likely to shape the technical and data standards of future EU tokenised bonds, green bonds and similar assets.

items.title: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority formally launches the CMU Digital Asset Platform: bond tokenisation, atomic DvP and 24-hour multi-currency settlement, with a next step toward funds and real-world assets
items.what: On 25 November the Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced the formal launch of the CMU Digital Asset Platform (CMU DAP), developed and operated by CMU OmniClear. The DLT platform covers a paperless end-to-end process for primary issuance of debt securities, secondary-trade clearing and settlement, interest payments and maturity redemption, and supports tokenisation of traditional bonds. It uses an on-chain atomic delivery-versus-payment (DvP) model, connecting directly to the real-time gross settlement (RTGS) system and central-bank digital currency, and supports 24-hour multi-currency settlement with cash tokens. CMU OmniClear's roadmap includes extending the platform from debt securities to funds and real-world assets, and connecting it to other DLT platforms and to payment instruments such as tokenised deposits and regulated stablecoins. HKMA Chief Executive Eddie Yue said the aim is to build CMU into core infrastructure of Hong Kong's multi-asset digital-finance ecosystem.
items.why: This is Hong Kong's first tokenised-bond platform operated by central-bank-grade financial infrastructure, and it explicitly writes "real-world assets" into the expansion roadmap. Combined with last week's Ensemble × Swift cooperation on cross-border tokenised deposits, Hong Kong now has a two-layer architecture of tokenised-asset registration and custody (CMU DAP) plus settlement in tokenised money (Ensemble).

items.tag: RWA · regulatory exemption in force (follow-up from last week)
items.title: OKXICE tokenised-securities venue goes live under an SEC "innovation exemption": 113 assets confirmed in the first batch, 67 issuers file objection notices
items.what: On 23 November, OKXICE, a joint venture of OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), announced that its tokenised-securities venue (TSV) had gone live, offering 24/7 trading to eligible US OKX users, with 113 confirmed assets (stocks, ETFs and ETPs) to be listed in stages. Issuers and asset managers include Fidelity, Coinbase, Circle, Robinhood and Securitize. Each token is a 1:1 securities interest backed by the underlying share, with shareholder rights including dividends and votes. Trading takes place in Uniswap v4 automated-market-maker liquidity pools on X Layer (an Ethereum layer 2), with smart contracts limiting eligible wallets, Securitize providing on-chain infrastructure, and assets self-custodied by users. The venue operates under a five-year temporary "innovation exemption" issued by the SEC on 17 September, and is not a registered exchange. According to The Block, citing the latest announcement, 67 companies have filed issuer objection notices, including Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia and Tesla, whose shares may not trade on the venue.
items.why: This is one of the first on-chain securities venues to go live in the United States under the SEC exemption framework (the SEC list shows that five institutions had filed TSV operating notices as of 23 November). A large number of leading issuers have chosen to object, showing that the key constraint on tokenisation in the United States is not only regulatory permission, but also issuer consent and the protection of shareholder rights.
items.src: OKX (OKXICE official) / The Block / SEC Innovation Exemption page

items.title: UK STEP awards a £6.84 million contract for design of a multi-stage depressed-collector gyrotron; Proxima Fusion completes manufacture of the first stellarator radial plate
items.what: The UK public-procurement platform Find a Tender announced on 24 November that UK Fusion Energy Limited had awarded a contract for design and manufacturability development of a "multi-stage depressed-collector gyrotron for fusion" on the STEP programme. The suppliers are Microwave Power Products, Inc and MuWave Limited, the contract value is £6.84 million including VAT, the expected term is 8 December 2026 to 31 March 2029, and the standstill period runs to 4 December. In the same period, World Nuclear News reported on 25 November that the first radial plate of Proxima Fusion's stellarator model coil had been manufactured: Rolf Kind supplied the base material, Pro Beam did the electron-beam welding and Mühlbauer the precision machining, all three members of its Alpha Alliance of more than 50 industrial partners. The coil is a key milestone toward the net-energy-gain demonstration device Alpha and the first plant, Stellaris.
items.why: After last week's METI subsidies in Japan and STEP procurement in the UK, European fusion this week again advanced through specific components and domestic manufacturing partners. Gyrotrons (for plasma heating) and three-dimensional, irregular superconducting-magnet structures are both critical bottlenecks for fusion plants, and supply-chain capability is becoming the focus of competition.
items.src: UK Find a Tender (UK Fusion Energy Limited) / World Nuclear News

items.title: Tennessee's first IRIS grant: $5.8 million for Type One Energy and the University of Tennessee to develop tritium-breeding ceramic pebbles; California awards $1.48 million for fusion technician training
items.what: On 23 November, Tennessee Governor Bill Lee and the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development (TNECD) announced that the first Innovation and Research for Industrial Success (IRIS) grant had been awarded to Type One Energy and the University of Tennessee, Knoxville: a two-year project to develop a new class of coated ceramic breeding pebbles to address production and management of tritium fuel for fusion plants. Total R&D spending is $5.8 million, of which $2.9 million is company funding and $2.9 million a state grant, supporting its commercial fusion-plant project, Project Infinity, under development in Clinton, Tennessee. On 24 November, the University of California San Diego announced $1.48 million from the California Workforce Development Board for a 12-week "Fusion Materials Technician" certificate programme at its Fusion Engineering Institute, free for the first cohort.
items.why: US support for fusion is moving down from the federal to the state level, and is taking two practical forms — 1:1 company matching funds, and non-degree technician training — corresponding respectively to the tritium-breeding fuel-cycle threshold for commercialisation and to a supply-chain labour shortage.
items.src: Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development / UC San Diego
